rating_scale: High = the option fully meets the criterion for this project; Medium = partly meets it, or only with extra effort; Low = does not meet it. Ratings are qualitative judgements against the project's own constraints (10 weeks, five students, no new ethics approval, eight assessment types, client deliverables D1 to D3), not scores.

decisions.decision: Review type for the evidence base (D1)
criteria: Fit to the research questions (evaluate and recommend)
Fit to mixed, mostly descriptive evidence
Feasible in 10 weeks with five people

options.option: Structured systematic review with narrative/framework synthesis (chosen)
options.note: Explicit criteria, dual screening and PRISMA reporting give rigour; synthesis copes with heterogeneous designs.
Maps the field but does not appraise quality or support graded recommendations [Arksey & O'Malley 2005; Grant & Booth 2009].
Fast, but selection is not reproducible; we borrowed one rapid-review method only (light extraction) [Garritty et al. 2021].
Needs comparable effect sizes; no included computing redesign study had a control group, so pooling was not possible.

decisions.choice_and_justification: A structured systematic review, reported with PRISMA 2020 [Page et al. 2021], was the only option rated at least Medium on all five criteria. It is the method the proposal committed to and it supports the graded ratings the client needs.
decisions.trade_off: Higher workload than a scoping review. Reduced by AI-assisted screening with human adjudication and by proportionate (light) extraction for non-computing studies.

decisions.decision: Synthesis method for the Evaluation Framework (D2)
criteria: Produces the required matrix (type x dimension)

options.option: Framework synthesis with a priori dimensions (chosen)
options.note: Dimensions taken from the proposal, Project Context and the data lead's framework; each cell traced to studies [Gale et al. 2013].
Themes emerge inductively, so they do not map cleanly onto the agreed assessment types and dimensions [Thomas & Harden 2008].
Ignores study quality and size.
Not possible without comparable effect sizes (see M1).

decisions.choice_and_justification: Framework synthesis fits a pre-defined matrix and keeps every rating traceable.
decisions.trade_off: Pre-set dimensions can miss new themes, so evidence gaps are listed for each type.

criteria: Suited to mixed and qualitative evidence

options.option: Adapted MMAT 2018 / CASP checklist plus simplified GRADE-CERQual (chosen)
options.note: MMAT covers qualitative, quantitative and mixed designs [Hong et al. 2018]; CERQual rates confidence in synthesis findings [Lewin et al. 2018].
Designed for effect estimates from trials, which this evidence lacks.
Would make all studies count equally regardless of quality.

decisions.choice_and_justification: The only option rated High on all four criteria.
decisions.trade_off: Both tools are simplified (5-item checklist; rule-based confidence), which the report states.

criteria: Scales to the update search (494 records)

options.option: Two independent AI-assisted screeners with human adjudication (chosen)
options.note: Kappa 0.80 to 0.88; every decision logged with a reason; disagreements adjudicated by a team member.
Standard practice, but not feasible for 586 records in the remaining weeks.
No agreement measure; higher risk of missed studies.

decisions.choice_and_justification: Kept dual, independent screening with a measurable agreement statistic while fitting the timeline. AI assistance is disclosed as an ethical requirement.
decisions.trade_off: AI screeners can share systematic biases; reduced by blinding, written criteria, human adjudication and full-text checks.

criteria: Direct evidence on GenAI and assessment

options.note: Released data with licences; our code reproduces every figure.

options.option: Primary data (surveys or interviews at Adelaide University)
options.note: Most direct, but needs human research ethics approval and recruitment time beyond a 10-week project.
Misses the chance to test claims against real student and AI data.

decisions.choice_and_justification: Public datasets added real behavioural evidence (StudyChat links AI use to grades) without ethics delay.
decisions.trade_off: Datasets come from other institutions and contexts; findings are labelled observational and context-specific.

options.note: GPT-3.5/GPT-4 on 5,175 real university questions; CC BY-NC-ND; a floor on AI capability.
2025/26 capstone; student and client views; self-report only.
Real student prompts linked to grades; CC BY 4.0.
2022, before GenAI; cannot inform GenAI vulnerability.
Considered in the Project Context; not linked to assessment outcomes.

decisions.choice_and_justification: The three chosen datasets cover what AI can do (EPFL), what students and clients say (Hannover) and what students actually do (StudyChat).
decisions.trade_off: EPFL models are from 2023, so exposure is likely understated; this is stated in every related cell.

criteria: Fits research tasks of uncertain length

options.option: Kanban in Jira (chosen in the proposal)
options.note: Continuous flow suits searching, screening and analysis whose duration is hard to predict.
Fixed sprints and ceremonies add overhead for a part-time student team.
Sequential stages cannot absorb changes such as the approved scope change.

decisions.choice_and_justification: Kanban was chosen in the proposal and suited a research workflow with an approved mid-project scope change.
decisions.trade_off: Kanban has no fixed deadlines inside the flow, so milestones were tracked separately in the Gantt chart. Actual use is reflected on in the project management section (team data needed).
